references.text: The preceding context where Jesus says, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" ([ref:Joh 2:19-20|John 2:19-20]). Verse 21 explains that Jesus was speaking of his own body, not the physical temple in Jerusalem.

The following verse tells us that after the resurrection, the disciples remembered this and believed both the Scripture and what Jesus had said ([ref:Joh 2:22|John 2:22]). The resurrection confirmed that Jesus was indeed speaking about the temple of his body.

John writes that "the Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us" ([ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14]). The Greek word for "made his dwelling" (ἐσκήνωσεν) carries connotations of the tabernacle, showing that God took up residence in Jesus' body—the new temple.

At Jesus' trial, some gave false testimony and said, "We heard him say, 'I will destroy this temple made with human hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands'" ([ref:Mark 14:58|Mark 14:58]). This refers back to Jesus' statement in John 2:19, which verse 21 explains was about his body.

Paul writes that "in him all the fullness of Deity lives in bodily form" ([ref:Kol 2:9|Colossians 2:9]). This emphasizes that the fullness of God dwells in Christ's body, explaining why Jesus could refer to his body as the temple.

Paul uses the same image as Jesus and calls the body a temple for the Holy Spirit: "Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit?" ([ref:1 Kor 6:19|1 Corinthians 6:19]). This confirms that God's temple can refer to the believer's body.

Hebrews refers to Jesus' body as the curtain leading to a "new and living way" into the holy place ([ref:Hebr 10:19-20|Hebrews 10:19-20]). Here, Jesus' body is directly connected with the temple concept and access to God.

Jesus says, "here is something greater than the temple" ([ref:Matt 12:6|Matthew 12:6]). Jesus points to himself as one who surpasses the physical temple, which aligns with John's explanation that Jesus was speaking of his own body as the temple.

In the new Jerusalem there is no temple, "for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple" ([ref:Åp 21:22|Revelation 21:22]). This shows the ultimate fulfillment that God himself—through Christ—is the true temple.
